name: Glioblastoma (high-grade glioma)
mri_findings: Irregular mass with thick, nodular or ring-like enhancement and a central necrotic core. Extensive T2/FLAIR hyperintense surrounding edema and infiltration. Mass effect and midline shift are common. May cross the corpus callosum (butterfly pattern). Heterogeneous signal, possible hemorrhage.
differential: Brain metastasis, brain abscess, primary CNS lymphoma, tumefactive demyelination.
next_steps: Contrast MRI with perfusion and MR spectroscopy, neurosurgical consultation, biopsy or resection for histology and molecular markers, tumor board.

name: Low-grade diffuse glioma
mri_findings: Infiltrative T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesion, T1 hypointense, usually little or no contrast enhancement and minimal surrounding edema. Poorly defined margins, mild mass effect. Calcification possible (oligodendroglioma).
differential: Ischemic infarct (subacute), encephalitis, gliomatosis cerebri, early high-grade glioma.
next_steps: Contrast MRI, MR spectroscopy/perfusion, follow-up imaging, neurosurgical evaluation, histology and IDH/1p19q status.

name: Meningioma
mri_findings: Extra-axial, dural-based, well-circumscribed mass. Iso-intense to gray matter on T1 and T2. Avid, homogeneous contrast enhancement with a dural tail. CSF cleft between mass and brain. Possible adjacent hyperostosis, calcification, or peritumoral edema.
differential: Dural metastasis, hemangiopericytoma/solitary fibrous tumor, lymphoma, neurosarcoidosis.
next_steps: Contrast MRI, evaluate venous sinus involvement, observation if small and asymptomatic, neurosurgery or radiosurgery referral if symptomatic or growing.

name: Pituitary adenoma
mri_findings: Sellar mass, macroadenomas (>10 mm) often with figure-of-eight or snowman shape extending to the suprasellar region and possibly compressing the optic chiasm. Enhances less than normal pituitary tissue. Microadenomas (<10 mm) appear hypoenhancing on dynamic contrast. Cavernous sinus invasion possible.
differential: Rathke cleft cyst, craniopharyngioma, meningioma, pituitary hyperplasia, aneurysm.
next_steps: Dedicated pituitary protocol MRI, hormonal laboratory work-up, visual field testing, endocrinology and neurosurgery referral.

name: Acute ischemic stroke
mri_findings: Hyperintense on DWI with low ADC (restricted diffusion) in a vascular territory. FLAIR may be normal in the first hours (DWI-FLAIR mismatch), later becoming hyperintense. Possible vessel occlusion on MRA, swelling and loss of gray-white differentiation.
differential: Hypoglycemia, seizure-related changes, tumor, abscess, demyelination, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome.
next_steps: Time-critical stroke pathway: confirm onset time, MRA/CTA for vessel occlusion, perfusion imaging, assess thrombolysis or thrombectomy eligibility, cardiac and vascular work-up.

name: Multiple sclerosis
mri_findings: Multiple ovoid T2/FLAIR hyperintense white-matter lesions, periventricular and perpendicular to the ventricles (Dawson fingers), also juxtacortical, infratentorial and spinal cord lesions. Active lesions enhance (nodular or open-ring). Chronic lesions may appear as T1 black holes.
differential: Small-vessel ischemic disease, neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, MOGAD, ADEM, vasculitis, migraine-related lesions.
next_steps: Contrast MRI of brain and spinal cord, apply McDonald criteria, CSF oligoclonal bands, aquaporin-4 and MOG antibodies, neurology referral.

name: Brain metastases
mri_findings: Often multiple enhancing lesions at the gray-white junction, round, with disproportionate vasogenic edema relative to size. Ring or solid enhancement. Hemorrhage possible (melanoma, renal, thyroid, choriocarcinoma).
next_steps: Contrast MRI of the whole brain, search for primary tumor (CT chest/abdomen/pelvis), oncology and radiation oncology or neurosurgery referral.

name: Brain abscess
mri_findings: Ring-enhancing lesion with a smooth, thin wall that is often thinner on the ventricular side. Central cavity shows markedly restricted diffusion (bright on DWI, low ADC). Surrounding vasogenic edema. Dual rim sign on susceptibility imaging.
differential: Necrotic glioblastoma, metastasis, tumefactive demyelination, resolving hematoma.
next_steps: Urgent clinical correlation (fever, infection source), blood cultures, neurosurgical aspiration or drainage, targeted antibiotics.

name: Normal brain MRI
mri_findings: Symmetric brain parenchyma, normal gray-white differentiation, no abnormal signal, no restricted diffusion, no abnormal enhancement, no mass effect or midline shift, normal ventricular size.
differential: Subtle or early disease not visible on the sequences provided.
next_steps: Correlate with clinical findings; consider additional sequences or follow-up if symptoms persist.
